metadata.case_name: CHAND LOK KUMAR v. LEIGHTON - LNS JOINT VENTURE

plaintiff.occupation_before: miner and leader of a team of 10 to 15 workers (tunnel worker); duties included connecting and installing pipe works, concrete plastering and setting up metal forms inside tunnels
plaintiff.occupation_after: security guard (part-time from 2014-2015; full-time from January 2016)

injuries.description: Comminute fracture in the middle phalanx of the right index finger; fractured shaft of right index finger middle phalanx with ulnar deviation of distal fragment with a butterfly fragment.
source: comminute fracture in the middle phalanx of the right index finger.
fractured shaft of right index finger middle phalanx with ulnar deviation of distal fragment with a butterfly fragment.

manifestations.description: Residual right index finger numbness (noted by plaintiff; judge noted numbness had gone except perhaps for some time after he wakes up in the morning)
Weak hand-grip / reduced power grip strength of right hand (measured over time)
Pain in the right index finger, including pain upon exertion
Tenderness in the scar of the right index finger
Reduced pincer / pinch grip strength of the right hand
Adhesion causing reduced range of movement of the right index finger (addressed by tenolysis)

treatments_received: open reduction and internal fixation with plates and screws (performed on 2014-01-13)
follow-up appointments at Queen Mary Hospital and David Trench Rehabilitation Centre

losses.description: Small degree of physical impairment of whole person (experts assessed 2% to 4%); residual impairment to right index finger including numbness, weak hand-grip and pain.
